items.q: What does David Park mean by fail at what you love?
items.a: You can **always fail**, including at a job you do not love. So fail at the thing you want. The sad truth is **not** that you will fail — long enough horizon and you can probably make a living. The sad truth is **boring days**.

items.q: Where is the billion-dollar blueprint, if not in gut instinct?
items.a: **Ripped up and scattered** in the users you are building for. Be **egotistical enough** to believe $1B is possible and **humble enough** to keep asking. Put the ego down.

items.q: What should you ask on a rare early user call?
items.a: Not 'what's your favorite thing?' That is a mood boost. Ask **current workflow**, **biggest pain**, and the **bad** things. Users are polite. Some lie. **Judge actions.**

items.q: How did Jenni get clearer as they shipped?
items.a: They **removed** features. Vision sharpened. KPI: first **autocomplete in five minutes**. A wave of users were already **students/researchers** — they kept building for the people who already got value.

items.q: What did the $100K actually buy them?
items.a: A flight to **Malaysia** (about **1/4** the cost) so they would not die. Still **~$2k MRR for 1.5–2 years**. Raise is not the success feeling. The viral tweet plus Intercom triage was.

items.q: Why does he say a founder needs more discipline than a 9-to-5?
items.a: People **bet on you**. He stayed out late, Google-Translated a Korean legal doc until 3 a.m., showed up late, and **lost a $250K done deal** with two months of runway and an engineer with a baby. Act like you took the leverage.

items.q: What happened when they finally peeked above the clouds?
items.a: **Thyroid cancer.** Eight years of 000, then the email. Fever, ice packs, mom's verse, same Bible verse on the ceiling. The void years hurt more than today's fires. Be ready for **years of unsexy reps**.
